content.title: Thrombolytic agents — dosing and contraindications

agents.name: rtPA (recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator)
agents.accelerated_regimen_note: Accelerated regimen mentioned in footnote for pulmonary embolism (used in extreme haemodynamic instability such as cardiac arrest); not officially approved.
contraindications: History of haemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin
Major trauma, surgery, or head injury in previous 3 weeks
agents.other_notes: Abbreviation defined on page: rtPA = recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator.

agents.name: Streptokinase
agents.dosing: 250,000 IU as a loading dose over 30 min, followed by 100,000 IU/h over 12–24 h
contraindications_absolute: History of haemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin
Major trauma, surgery, or head injury in previous 3 weeks
contraindications_relative: Transient ischaemic attack in previous 6 months

agents.name: Urokinase
agents.dosing: 4,400 IU/kg as a loading dose over 10 min, followed by 4,400 IU/kg/h over 12–24 h

content.footnote: This is the accelerated regimen for rtPA in pulmonary embolism; it is not officially approved, but it is sometimes used in extreme haemodynamic instability such as cardiac arrest. Unclear whether early thrombolysis for intermediate- or high-risk acute PE has an impact on long-term outcomes; small randomized trial suggested possible improvement in functional capacity at 3 months compared with anticoagulation alone.

Associated Conditions: Pulmonary embolism (use of rtPA for thrombolysis)
Haemodynamic instability / cardiac arrest (context of accelerated rtPA use)
genes.context: Page defines rtPA as recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator and discusses an accelerated rtPA regimen for pulmonary embolism and extreme haemodynamic instability.
